examples.trans: That can't be.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to buy', paired with 'покупать'.

examples.text: Костя, можно было не как у меня телефон купить?
examples.trans: Kostya, could you not have bought the exact same phone as mine?

examples.text: Думаешь, мы не можем купить, сколько стоит?
examples.trans: Do you think we cannot buy it, how much does it cost?

examples.text: Вот, смотри, я купила у Евы машину!
examples.trans: Here, look, I bought the car from Eva!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'колько'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Думаешь, мы не можем купить, сколько стоит?
examples.trans: Do you think we cannot buy it, how much does it cost?

examples.text: Буквально несколько капель для вкуса, понял?
examples.trans: Literally just a few drops for flavor, got it?

examples.text: Сколько жвачки!
examples.trans: So much gum!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тоять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is standing', paired with 'постоять'.

examples.text: И запомни, Дима, кухня — это настоящая магия!
examples.trans: And remember, Dima, the kitchen is real magic!

examples.text: Кухня — это настоящая магия!
examples.trans: The kitchen is real magic!

examples.text: А всё почему, потому что я настоящий гений!
examples.trans: And why is that, because I am a true genius!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'five hundred', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Пятьсот пятьдесят тысяч рублей.
examples.trans: Five hundred and fifty thousand rubles.

examples.text: Это стоит пятьсот рублей.
examples.trans: It costs five hundred roubles.

examples.text: Рублей пятьсот.
examples.trans: About five hundred roubles.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'fifty', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Пятьсот пятьдесят тысяч рублей.
examples.trans: Five hundred and fifty thousand rubles.

examples.text: Настя, мне только что премию дали, пятьдесят тысяч!
examples.trans: Nastya, they just gave me a bonus, fifty thousand!

examples.text: И тебе тоже пятьдесят тысяч, Вика перед уходом наградила!
examples.trans: And fifty thousand for you too, Vika rewarded us before leaving!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'thousand' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Пятьсот пятьдесят тысяч рублей.
examples.trans: Five hundred and fifty thousand rubles.

examples.text: Костя, держи, вот тебе шестьсот тысяч.
examples.trans: Kostya, take this, here is six hundred thousand for you.

examples.text: Настя, мне только что премию дали, пятьдесят тысяч!
examples.trans: Nastya, they just gave me a bonus, fifty thousand!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'rubles' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Пятьсот пятьдесят тысяч рублей.
examples.trans: Five hundred and fifty thousand rubles.

examples.text: Это стоит сто рублей.
examples.trans: This costs a hundred roubles.

examples.text: У меня нет ни рубля.
examples.trans: I haven't got a single rouble.

meanings.en: a little bit, just a little
meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'a tiny bit', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У нас чуть-чуть не хватает, но мы подумаем.
examples.trans: We are a tiny bit short, but we will think about it.

examples.text: А ты плесни чуть-чуть масла на сковороду пока.
examples.trans: And you splash a tiny bit of oil into the pan for now.

examples.text: Нам нужно чуть-чуть потерпеть и немножко поработать.
examples.trans: We need to be patient a little and work a bit.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is enough, suffices', paired with 'схватить'.

examples.text: У нас чуть-чуть не хватает, но мы подумаем.
examples.trans: We are a tiny bit short, but we will think about it.

examples.text: Почему он меня хватает?
examples.trans: Why is he grabbing me?

examples.text: Не хватай меня!
examples.trans: Don't grab me!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Оно греет и влюблённую пару, и одинокого парня.
examples.trans: It warms both a couple in love and a lonely guy.

examples.text: Одинокого парня, который уже забыл, что такое солнце.
examples.trans: A lonely guy who has already forgotten what the sun is.

examples.text: Как же сильно я сегодня устал!
examples.trans: How exhausted I am today!

meanings.en: to think it over, to give it a thought
meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'умать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will think', paired with 'думать'.

examples.text: У нас чуть-чуть не хватает, но мы подумаем.
examples.trans: We are a tiny bit short, but we will think about it.

examples.text: Я подумаю.
examples.trans: I'll think about it.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.
